name: ARC_XCPU
default: on: discrete 16-lane cards (B-series, Max); off: Alchemist, iGPUs
title: CPU experts
what: A MoE model's experts that are not on the card are computed by the CPU from RAM instead of being copied over PCIe
cost: none (RAM the expert tier already uses)
measured: a B60 on PCIe 3.0 x8, Flash Next generation 22.5 -> 27.3-28.2 tok/s; an A770 on x16: no gain; the top token against f32 a little lower than off (a B60: 241 -> 237 of 256)
tip: The experts that are not on the card are computed by the CPU from their copy in RAM, instead of being sent over PCIe each time. This helps most when the card's PCIe link is slow or the model is much bigger than the card. Text can differ slightly (checked against full precision).

name: ARC_XCPU_Q2
title: CPU experts exact in precise mode
what: With Flash Next's precise mode, the CPU's experts run both passes too (default: one pass, faster)
cost: the CPU experts 0.302 instead of 0.187 ms each
measured: KL on 548 chat + 160 code positions 0.00076 / 0.00222 against one pass's 0.00126 / 0.00251; top token 702 against 700 of 708
tip: In Flash Next's precise mode, the CPU's experts also take the second, more exact pass. A little slower on the CPU's share, a little more exact.

name: ARC_140T_RES
title: Decoded weights kept for short prompts
what: On the Arc 140T and Alchemist cards: short prompt chunks use resident decoded weights, long ones decode just in time
cost: about 2x the weights' size in VRAM
measured: an Alchemist card under Linux, the 4B's 128-token prompt 1,161 -> 2,030 tok/s (skipzx-lab, PR #61)
conflicts: needs room for the weights twice
tip: On the Arc 140T and Arc A-series cards, short prompts use decoded weights kept on the card, while long prompts still decode them as they go. It needs room for the weights twice, so only on cards with memory to spare.

name: ARC_H8_MIN
title: Exact prompts on Lunar Lake / Panther Lake
what: Prompts read without the H8 rotation on iGPUs with 16-lane XMX (Arc 140V, B390): a little more exact, slower
measured: the 27B's top token 473 against 470 of 480 against f32 (the laptop, the B390 / 140V path)
tip: On Lunar Lake and Panther Lake, prompts are read without the H8 rotation. A little more exact, and prompts of 256 to 1,023 tokens are 1.4 to 1.8 times slower.

name: ARC_H8_Q2
title: More precise prompt reading
what: Reads the prompt with a second int8 pass that carries what the first one rounds away, so the prompt is read much closer to full precision. About half the prompt speed on GPUs without XMX, less of a slowdown on XMX cards. Generation is unchanged. It runs wherever H8 does (B-series, Alchemist, the 140T, Lunar Lake / Panther Lake)
measured: the laptop (no XMX), the 27B on 480 tokens against f32: KL 0.00112 -> 0.00061 (plain 0.00056), top token 467 -> 474 of 480; its 4K prompt 117 -> 62 tok/s
tip: The prompt is read in two int8 passes, the second carrying what the first rounds away, so it is read much closer to full precision. Prompts are slower (about half the speed without XMX), and generation is unchanged.

name: ARC_FN_PRECISE
title: Precise mode
what: Flash Next's exact mode, its default since 2026-11-22: two int8 passes, f16 keys and values, the routers, hyper-connection and PLE rows in BF16 and the Q4_K / Q5_K prompt rows with their mins. Off (--fast, the variant -fast) is the fast mode: prompts about 1.7x as fast and a little faster generation, less exact on markdown and code. It combines with either attention mode
cost: off: prompts ~1.7x as fast, less exact
measured: KL against f32 on the laptop (2026-11-22): 480 tokens of markdown 0.0033 (fast mode 0.0415), 3,584 of prose 0.0073 (0.0109); 3,584-token prompt 74.8 tok/s (fast 127.7)
tip: Flash Next's exact mode, on by default. Turned off (the fast mode), prompts run about 1.7 times as fast, but code, tables and other markdown come out less exact.

name: --budget
default: the card's free memory, by the model
title: Resident weights
what: Keep the decoded weights on the card up to this many GiB, instead of decoding them for every prompt chunk
measured: a split 27B: the 512-token prompt 1,028 -> 1,481 tok/s, but the 4K prompt slower (manoreken2, #4)
tip: Keeps the decoded weights on the card, up to this many GiB, so prompts don't decode them again for every chunk. It uses that much more GPU memory, which leaves less room for context.

name: ARC_TP_P2P
default: by the links: direct where it is faster
title: Multi-GPU sums
what: A split model's sums: 1 straight from GPU to GPU, 0 through host memory, prompt: direct for prompts only
measured: 4 Max 1550 stacks: prompt only direct, 512-token prompt 2,137 -> 2,548 tok/s (hibagus, #48)
tip: For a model split over several GPUs: how the GPUs add up their partial results, straight from card to card or through the PC's memory. The default picks by measuring the links. On means card to card for everything; ARC_TP_P2P=prompt (card to card for prompts only) is set from a terminal.

name: --copy-draft
title: Copy drafting
what: With --mtp: where the last tokens appeared earlier in the conversation, the tokens that followed are drafted; the same text
measured: a code edit on the laptop: the 27B 17.5 -> 22.1 tok/s, the 4B 42.0 -> 58.5; summaries unchanged
tip: With MTP drafting: where the last few tokens appeared earlier in the conversation, the tokens that came after them are tried as the draft. Edits of code or text you pasted go faster. The text stays the same.

name: ARC_MTP_VOCAB
title: Drafts from the common tokens (English and code)
what: With --mtp: each draft reads only the 32,768 most common tokens' rows of the output head, not all 248,320; the model still checks every draft against the full vocabulary, so the text stays the same
cost: 69 MB of GPU memory (the 4B; more with a wider model); Chinese text drafts less well (the laptop's 4B 31.6 -> 26.7 tok/s), Indonesian about even
measured: the laptop's 4B on a coding prompt 35.9-37.3 -> 44.3-45.8 tok/s, the 27B 10.9 -> 12.6; Indonesian 27.4 -> 28.9; Chinese 31.6 -> 26.7
tip: With MTP drafting: each draft looks only at the 32,768 most common tokens (the launchers' size; ARC_MTP_VOCAB from a terminal sets another), which makes drafting faster for English and code. Every draft is still checked against the full vocabulary, so the text stays the same. Chinese text drafts less well.

name: ARC_BATCH
default: 64 on Alchemist (Windows and Linux), off elsewhere
title: Kernels sent in lists
what: A token's kernels sent to the GPU in recorded lists instead of one by one
measured: an A750 on Linux (i915): the 4B 46.0 -> 66.6 tok/s, with MTP 68.4 -> 88.5 (hakangit, #72); an A770 on Linux (xe): no change (skipzx-lab, #45); two A770s on Windows 12.7 -> 21.6
tip: A token's GPU work is sent in recorded lists instead of one piece at a time, which saves time on the CPU's side. The text stays the same. The launchers set lists of up to 64; another size is set with ARC_BATCH from a terminal.

name: ARC_GEMV_GU
title: Gate and up in one launch
what: One token's FFN gate and up products in one kernel launch instead of two
measured: an A750: the 4B's generation +4.6 % alone, +2.5 % on top of ARC_BATCH (hakangit, #72)
tip: Each token's two FFN products, gate and up, run as one GPU launch instead of two. The text stays the same.

name: --split
default: tensor (each layer's matrices over the GPUs)
title: Multi-GPU by layers
what: With --gpus 2 or more: each GPU holds a range of the layers instead of a share of every layer, the rows passed from GPU to GPU; for a model one card cannot hold, or links too slow for the tensor split. --tensor-split a,b,... sets each GPU's share (GPU 0 holds the last layers)
cost: about one card's speed for one request (a token visits each GPU in turn)
measured: bit for bit against one GPU (ARC_TP_SIM, the 4B and 27B, 2 and 3 GPUs); an A770 pair not measured yet
conflicts: needs --gpus 2 or more; Qwen dense only; no --mtp, images, saved prompts or sessions yet
tip: With two or more GPUs: each GPU holds a range of the model's layers instead of a share of every layer. Use it for a model one card can't hold, cards of different kinds, or links too slow for the default split. One request runs at about one card's speed.

name: ARC_QSA
default: per model: the QSA 27B full attention, Flash Next sparse (its trained form)
title: Attention: sparse (on) or full (off)
what: For the two models with a trained attention indexer. Sparse: past 2,048 tokens of context each token reads only the 2,048 keys its indexer picks, faster on long prompts. Full: every key, the most exact. Shorter work is the same either way. The QSA 27B uses full attention unless this is on; Flash Next uses sparse, its trained form, unless this is off
cost: sparse is faster on long prompts, full is more exact
measured: the QSA 27B on 480 tokens, 64 keys: sparse against its own sparse f32 reference KL 0.0014, against the full one 0.0184. Flash Next, the last 256 of 3,584 tokens: full against its dense reference 0.00855, sparse against its sparse one 0.00914, the two forms ~0.011 apart. The speed of long prompts not measured yet
conflicts: the QSA 27B or Flash Next; not with --attn-f32 or --split layer (full attention there)
tip: For the two models trained with a sparse attention indexer (the QSA 27B and Flash Next). On: past 2,048 tokens each token reads only the 2,048 keys its indexer picks, faster on long prompts. Off: every key, the most exact.

name: ARC_MOE_BIG_CHUNK
title: Larger MoE prompt chunks
what: A standard MoE model's prompt in chunks of 16,384 tokens where that keeps the same context and every expert the GPU held (by default 8,192 by the same rule; off: 4,096)
cost: none where it applies: a chunk that would cost context or experts is not taken
measured: a B390's 35B 16K prompt 1,166 -> 1,714 tok/s (cjm801, #75) and 1,362-1,411 -> 1,692 (kludged, #74); the logits the same at each chunk
tip: Reads a mixture-of-experts model's prompt in bigger pieces, so its experts are prepared half as often. Taken only where it costs no context and keeps every expert on the GPU.
